response.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status

assumptions.assumption: Attendees are counted as attendance rows (event-member pairs) whose event exists; since the primary key is (event, member), each row is one attendance. A member attending events of the same status in multiple events is counted once per event.
Share is a fraction between 0 and 1 (not a percentage), computed against the total of matched attendance rows across all statuses.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct members per status (a member attending multiple events with the same status counted once); share is relative to the sum of those per-status distinct counts.
alternatives.sql: SELECT status, cnt AS attendee_count, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM (SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS cnt FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status)
